summary.headline: ESDS H1 FY27 revenue rose 24.6% YoY to INR 2,719 million; Q2 revenue INR 1,383.4 million, up 3.5% QoQ, with AI factory (Sharon AI) go-live pending.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 1,383.4 million, up 3.5% QoQ from INR 1,336.6 million in Q1. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 2,719 million (up 24.6% YoY), total income INR 2,788 million (up 25.6%), EBITDA INR 1,137.5 million (up 12.3%) and PAT INR 603.7 million (up 26.3%). Management said the main growth driver is the 8,200-GPU AI factory contracted with Sharon AI and sold to ESDS's customers, now in final testing with NVIDIA, with RFS targeted between early and 17 December. Management also flagged the CIO/CTO exits, a shrinking customer count, and that the 8,200 GPUs are priced at contracted rates and cannot be repriced upward.

+24.6% YoY vs INR 2,183.7 million in H1 FY26

INR 3,419.80 million, including ~INR 6,500 million of IPO-related FDs as stated
INR 469.13 million of INR 7,200 million; INR 6,730.87 million unutilised

segments.name: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
segments.commentary: Described as the foundation of the business, covering data centre, cloud, colocation, AI compute and AI factories. Domestic revenue was cited as about INR 500 crores, with management aiming to triple or quadruple it in 1-2 years. Data centre utilisation is about 85%.

segments.name: Managed services
segments.commentary: Management said the managed services and SaaS funnel is less promising than the AI infrastructure funnel at present. No segment-level figures were given.

segments.name: Software as a Service (Swaraj)
segments.commentary: Swaraj portfolio spans cybersecurity, observability and automation. Management expects DPDP Act enforcement next year to drive demand, with a domestic cloud and colocation opportunity of about INR 3,000 crores. No revenue figure was disclosed.

segments.name: Cloud services and customer base
segments.commentary: An analyst cited cloud services down 9% QoQ, infrastructure down 4% and BFSI revenue down, with customers falling from 2,216 to 1,709. Management said small customers are being moved to a virtual subsidiary, the company is targeting 400-500 core customers, and about 50-60 customers were asked to exit.

guidance_outlook: Sharon AI 8,200-GPU AI factory: NVIDIA cluster testing expected to finish within 2-3 weeks; hand-over to NVIDIA by 27 November at the latest, then 20 days of customer testing; RFS between the first week of December and 17 December.
Management expects to book one month of revenue and profit in Q3 FY27 and a full quarter in Q4 FY27.

Once live, the Sharon AI project is expected to bill about INR 288 crores per month and earn about INR 50-60 crores of PAT per month (domestic margin 26-27%, AI factory margin 16-18%). Annualised revenue was put at about INR 3,000 crores, which management described as the liability to Sharon AI.

India: INR 1,500 crores of capex, funded from IPO proceeds and customer advances, to add about 1,150-1,200 GPUs by June-July 2027, targeting about INR 1,000 crores of annual revenue; further additions expected August-September 2027.
Pipeline of about INR 3,000 crores for India. Overseas GPU pipeline (about 50,000 GPUs previously referenced) is under negotiation with partners in the US, South Korea, Taiwan and Sweden (MoU).
capex_capacity: Sharon AI AI factory: 8,200 GPUs and about 16 MW power in a single Sydney data centre, fully contracted to ESDS on a take-or-pay basis; ESDS's commitment to Sharon AI is for 5 years, with the rate locked for 7 years (about 30-40% below the customer price for the first five years).
India: capex of INR 1,500 crores from IPO proceeds plus customer advances, targeting go-live by June 2027 (smaller AI factory, about 1,150-1,200 GPUs).
Three further India data centres to add capacity, expected to be operational in the next two to three months. Current utilisation is about 85%.
Management is acquiring data centres with 50-100 MW power capability (powered land) and aims to bring 1 GW of power under its control.
demand_pricing: Sharon AI GPUs were contracted at about USD 3.50/hour; management said current B300 market rates are about USD 7/hour, but ESDS cannot reprice its customer contracts, which are locked for 5 years.
Management said that at current prices the project could have earned about INR 150 crores of PAT a month, but the existing commitments rule out a price increase.
AI factory demand comes from 17-18 leading AI labs; banks are also a buyer. Management said pricing will improve at renewal as capacity grows.
Management cited power shortages in the US, Europe and Australia as the reason overseas customers may move capacity to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Sharon AI GPU commissioning, and what revenue and margin will it contribute in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NVIDIA cluster testing is in the final stage with RFS between early and 17 December 2026. Monthly revenue of about INR 288 crores and PAT of about INR 50-60 crores per month were given once live; the annual revenue run-rate was put at about INR 3,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a delay, and is there any funding issue at Sharon AI? What SLAs apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sharon AI is well capitalised with about USD 2 billion in cash against a market cap of about USD 1.5 billion, and that the delay is due to NVIDIA testing rigour. It did not give SLA terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CIO and CTO roles change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CAIO and CPO roles absorbed the CIO and CTO functions. CIO is now redundant and the company does not currently plan to hire a CTO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sharon AI contract structure: five or seven years?
qa_highlights.answer: The ESDS commitment to Sharon AI is for 5 years, with pricing locked for 7 years. Renewal after 5 years would be at the lower locked rate; ESDS's customer pricing is flexible after 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR 670 crore non-current and INR 1,900 crore current liabilities on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said these reflect a USD 140 million advance paid to Sharon AI and a matching customer advance, both amortised on a mirrored schedule, so the liability and asset line up.

qa_highlights.question: What are the India capex, capacity and revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 1,500 crores of capex will add about 1,150-1,200 GPUs by June-July 2027, targeting about INR 1,000 crores of annual revenue. The India pipeline is INR 3,000 crores, mainly IaaS for defence PSUs, government and enterprises.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any international design revenue in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said there was no international design revenue in Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Sharon AI go-live timing: any NVIDIA or customer testing slippage beyond mid-December would delay the first revenue month, which management guided for Q3.
Pricing gap: market GPU rates (about USD 7/hour) are well above the contracted rate (about USD 3.50/hour), so ESDS cannot capture current pricing on the locked contracts.
Counterparty dependence on Sharon AI: the 5-year liability of about INR 3,000 crores a year sits against a single supplier, and no SLA terms were disclosed.
Management and org changes: the CTO and CIO resigned and no replacement is planned; the company is also exiting small customers.
Customer churn: the customer count fell from 2,216 to 1,709 per an analyst's figures, and management plans to drop more customers.
Capital deployment: only about INR 469 million of the INR 7,200 million IPO proceeds has been utilised so far.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the AI factory opportunity, with forecasts given freely. Evasive on specifics: it declined to disclose Sharon AI SLA terms or per-GPU-hour pricing, and deflected questions on the CTO exit and the balance-sheet liabilities.

We are lucky that we identified them as our partner very early because now the same B300 rates are being quoted at $7 an hour.
We are trying to keep only 400 -500 customers in ESDS, not more than that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Sharon AI bills about INR 288 crore/month with PAT of INR 50-60 crore/month once live (AI factory margin 16-18% vs domestic 26-27%), so one month in Q3 and a full quarter in Q4 lift reported profitability, though the AI factory margin is lower than domestic.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sharon AI 8,200-GPU, ~16 MW Sydney factory is in NVIDIA testing with RFS by 17 Dec 2026, and three further India data centres are under construction and expected to be operational in the next 2-3 months, with utilisation at about 85%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Sharon AI take-or-pay contract starts billing with one month of revenue in Q3 and a full quarter in Q4 FY27, against Q2 revenue of INR 1,383.4 million (+3.5% QoQ), so the step-up is contracted rather than demand-dependent.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR 1,500 crore India capex is already committed (IPO proceeds plus customer advances) for 1,150-1,200 GPUs, utilisation is 85%, and management is acquiring 50-100 MW powered land aiming for 1 GW, so further capex announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on Sharon AI billing and sees India GPU revenue of INR 1,000 crore/year from Jun-Jul 2027, but the contracted rate is locked, so any upgrade depends on RFS landing by mid-December.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sharon AI RFS is set for early to 17 December 2026 with testing slippage flagged as a risk; any slip beyond mid-December would push the first billing month out of Q3, and customers fell from 2,216 to 1,709.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects DPDP Act enforcement next year to drive Swaraj SaaS demand (domestic cloud/colocation opportunity ~INR 3,000 crore), but no launch date or revenue was disclosed.

rows.label: India AI pipeline of ~INR 3,000 crore
rows.why: Pipeline of about INR 3,000 crore is mainly IaaS for defence PSUs, government and enterprises, but no contracts were announced on the call.

rows.label: Overseas GPU pipeline (~50,000 GPUs referenced)
rows.why: Negotiations are under way with partners in the US, South Korea, Taiwan and Sweden (MoU), with power shortages in the US, Europe and Australia cited as a reason customers may shift capacity to India, but no signed deal was disclosed.

rows.label: IPO proceeds deployment
rows.why: INR 6,730.87 million of INR 7,200 million is unutilised, with the INR 1,500 crore India capex planned to be funded from it, so deployment should accelerate.
